name: Peacock Orchid
family: Iridaceae, the iris family (not an orchid)
grown_as: Grown from bought corms planted in spring. William's library calls it Gladiolus callianthus 'Acidanthera', an older name for the same plant.
habit: Upright fans of narrow sword leaves 50 to 70 cm, with slender flower stems 70 to 100 cm that arch at the top.

leaf.arrangement: In a flat fan, each leaf folded at the base and sitting astride the next
leaf.outline: 30 to 60 cm long by 1 to 2.5 cm wide, narrow and straight-sided, tapering to the tip
leaf.veins: A few strong parallel ribs, the midrib clearest, making the leaf look ribbed

flower.form: A starry white flower with a dark purple eye, hanging on a long thin tube
flower.petals: Six tepals, joined at the base into a long, slender, curved tube 8 to 12 cm; the tepals pointed oval and spreading into a star, slightly unequal
flower.colour: White, with a deep maroon-purple blotch at the base of each tepal
flower.centre: The blotches meet to make a dark star-shaped eye; three stamens and a branched style stand out of the throat
flower.behind: Two green, pointed spathes at the base of each flower's tube
flower.carried: Four to ten flowers in a loose, one-sided spike, nodding or held sideways, opening from the bottom up
flower.season: August to October; strongly scented in the evening

fruit: Rarely ripens in the UK. An oblong three-lobed green capsule that splits into three.
winter: Nothing above ground: corms are lifted in autumn and stored frost-free, or left under a deep mulch in mild gardens.

bloom: six pointed white tepals in a star
a dark maroon-purple blotch at the base of each, making a dark eye
a long thin curved tube behind
bulb: a corm, not a bulb: round and flattened, 2 to 3 cm
covered in a brown netted fibrous skin
a pointed shoot on top, roots from the base
shoots: a flat fan of pointed sword leaves coming up in late spring
leaves sitting astride each other in one flat plane, ribbed
flower: arching stems with several nodding white flowers with dark eyes
seedhead: three-lobed green pods along the stem
dormant: the corm, lifted or below ground

look_alikes: Garden gladioli have broad, ruffled, upward-facing flowers in a stiff one-sided spike and no dark eye on every tepal. Crocosmia leaves are pleated and its flowers orange. Not related to true orchids.
